ante-nicene.alt: Dura-Europos house church fresco of Christ healing the paralytic.
ante-nicene.caption: A third-century house church fresco from Dura-Europos, from the world before Constantine and Nicaea.
ante-nicene.credit: Yale University Art Gallery, via Wikimedia Commons

apologists.alt: Icon of Justin Martyr by Theophanes the Cretan.
apologists.caption: Justin Martyr represents the Christian turn toward public apology before emperors and philosophers.
apologists.credit: Theophanes the Cretan, via Wikimedia Commons

apostolic.alt: Good Shepherd fresco from the Catacomb of Priscilla.
apostolic.caption: The Good Shepherd fresco evokes the earliest Christian visual world downstream of the apostles.

apostolic-fathers.caption: A fourth-century biblical codex, a fitting visual for the age when apostolic teaching became a handed-on textual inheritance.

desert-fathers.alt: Entrance to Saint Anthony's cave at the Monastery of Saint Anthony in Egypt.
desert-fathers.caption: The cave of Saint Anthony, a concrete image of the desert as a place of prayer, struggle, and spiritual fatherhood.
desert-fathers.credit: Kazazian / Dumbarton Oaks, via Wikimedia Commons

early-medieval.alt: Carpet page from the Lindisfarne Gospels.
early-medieval.caption: Insular manuscript art points to the monastic copying culture that carried patristic learning into the early medieval West.

nicene.alt: Rylands papyrus fragment containing the Nicene Creed.
nicene.caption: The Rylands Nicene Creed papyrus gives the council age a textual face.

post-nicene.alt: Apse mosaic of the Virgin and Child in Hagia Sophia.
post-nicene.caption: Hagia Sophia's apse mosaic belongs to the world of post-Chalcedonian liturgy, empire, and icon theology.
